markdown_report:
**Select causal, position-dependent depth aggregation inside NextItNet.** At 10% progress, this remains a feasible controlled adaptation. No new training results are available.

Three supplied insights guide it. Recent deletion reduces margins more than older deletion across categories, supporting context-sensitive modeling without proving harmful historical influence. Electronics has the highest sampled negative-win rate, 6.38%, motivating discrimination improvements without establishing HR@10 weakness. Users report stale preferences and broad matches displacing precise current choices; adaptive aggregation targets both, but cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs.

Three literature insights refine the mechanism. [Jumping Knowledge](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/xu18c/xu18c.pdf) and [Dynamic Layer Aggregation](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/3772/3650) directly precede input-dependent layer mixing, limiting originality. [ELMo](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1202/) supplies static softmax aggregation, making static versus dynamic conditioning an essential comparison. [Identity Mappings](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05027) motivates an alternative optimization explanation: intermediate readouts introduce shorter gradient paths.

| Direction | Mechanism | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Context selection | Dynamic depth gates; finer tap gates | Depth weights do not establish historical exclusion |
| Discrimination | Temperature-controlled candidate CE | False negatives and objective confounding |
| Item specificity | Joint title/description encoder | Text need not reveal current purpose |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment includes a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Depth gates** | 2: targeted transfer; direct precedents | 6: useful controlled study; incremental | 6: targets staleness and broad matches; purpose unobserved | 6: adaptive discrimination; healthy baseline | 4: small module; controls/export care |
| Causal tap gates | 5: finer selection; familiar gating | 7: individual lag selection; optimization risk | 7: suppresses irrelevant events; intent unobserved | 6: tests lag use; perturbations inconclusive | 7: local control; convolution rewrite |
| Joint text augmentation | 3: explicit distinctions; established fusion | 6: sparse-item features; noisy descriptions | 8: precise attributes; purpose unavailable | 5: richer scores; no semantic diagnosis | 6: simple pooling; vocabulary overhead |

Collect causal block outputs, normalize over channels, and aggregate using position-dependent softmax weights before the existing scoring head. This targets stale-interest persistence and broad historical matches outranking current specific preferences, while testing Electronics’ sampled discrimination weakness.

Shallow weights can depend on older inputs through deeper logits in the shared denominator. Treat weights as relative mixing coefficients, following [attention-interpretation cautions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10186), rather than explanations of exclusion.

Compare normalization-matched final-layer, uniform, static, and dynamic variants separately; add capacity controls only within budget. Track norms, gradients, gate variability, and paired value/routing interventions. Preserve the objective, benchmark constraints, one checkpoint/category, predictor consistency, diagnostic support counts, and qualitative rejection reasons. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; gains and user benefits remain hypotheses.

idea.description: Add a small causal softmax gate over intermediate residual-block features in the corrected NextItNet. At each sequence position, the gate learns how much each dilation depth contributes to one feature vector, followed by the existing item-scoring head. All components are jointly trained within one network per category. Frame this as an incremental adaptation of established dynamic layer aggregation, not a new intent-identification or historical-exclusion mechanism.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly addresses two reported user failures: older or occasional preferences outweighing current preferences, and broadly related historical interests displacing more specific current matches. Different depths offer different contextual representations, so adaptive aggregation may help choose useful evidence without discarding longer history globally. The quantitative target is Electronics’ relatively weak sampled discrimination: a 6.38% negative-win rate and 0.4364 tenth-percentile margin across 988 positions. These are diagnostic comparisons, not benchmark HR@10, and do not prove that historical context causes errors. Embedding scores near 0.5 provide no justification for a collapse intervention. Existing recent-history sensitivity argues against assuming that the baseline ignores recent events. At 10% progress, retain this small experiment ahead of causal tap rewrites or a text pipeline, provided the essential static and normalization controls fit the remaining budget. Joint text augmentation remains a plausible later direction for explicit item distinctions; it cannot establish current purpose or actual compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration proposal: the corrected baseline source was not included in the supplied text, so a complete executable train.py cannot be reconstructed reliably. No filesystem inspection, training, or validation was performed. The concrete baseline constructor, optimizer settings, batch size, sequence length, precision, sampling details, validation schedule, checkpoint rule, empty-history policy, and remaining GPU budget must come from the host-supplied baseline before implementation. Preserve and record those values; the proposal does not claim an independently executable reproduction.

Preserve the supplied NextItNet blocks, their causal ordering, item embeddings, sampler, objective, optimizer, and checkpoint policy for the initial architectural comparison. Collect the eight block outputs reported by the supplied topology. Their structural receptive-field spans are 5, 13, 29, 61, 65, 73, 89, and 121 for the reported kernel-3, same-dilation convolution pairs. Compute these values from the actual implementation rather than assuming this topology universally. Depth is not a clean separation of recent and older evidence: deeper states retain short paths through residual connections. The actual baseline topology, rather than the generic original NextItNet block description, determines these spans.

For depth d and position t, let z[d,t] be channel-normalized block features. Use gate logits a[d,t] = w[d]^T z[d,t] + b[d], followed by softmax over depths. Initialize w and b to zero, giving uniform aggregation. Form h[t] = sum_d alpha[d,t] * z[d,t], then apply the baseline final normalization/scoring pathway consistently. Start with one shared affine LayerNorm across intermediate depths, using the baseline normalization epsilon; it computes separate channel statistics for each position and depth while sharing gain and bias. Record epsilon and affine settings in the checkpoint configuration. This retains the original shared-normalization proposal while making its control requirements explicit. Independent affine parameters could let layers rescale their contributions and complicate weight interpretation, so they are not part of the initial experiment. Normalization changes gradients as well as activation scales; even a shared affine map does not make gate weights an explanation of score contributions.

Padded positions remain zero before temporal convolutions and after sublayers, blocks, normalization, and aggregation. Gate values at padded positions are excluded from summaries. Do not add absolute padded-position features or future-dependent pooling. The gate uses only block outputs at the current position, whose computations are causal. Training targets must remain strictly after their corresponding input prefixes; no target token is inserted into its own context.

A shallow representation has a bounded local receptive field, but its softmax weight need not. For alpha_d = exp(a_d)/sum_j exp(a_j), an older input outside depth d can still alter alpha_d through deeper logits in the denominator. The aggregated feature therefore has the union of value and routing dependencies, reaching the deepest collected representation under this topology. Detaching deep logits changes gradients but leaves their forward historical dependence intact. Large shallow weights indicate relative mixing preference, not exclusion of older history. A fixed shallow-only readout tests bounded context only when all its upstream computations, including normalization and routing, are themselves local. Neither a zero local Jacobian nor unchanged top-k results proves historical irrelevance.

Use a prespecified sequential comparison rather than a normalization-by-aggregation factorial sweep. Retain the corrected baseline as the reference. First evaluate final-depth-only with the same additional shared normalization and baseline output pathway used by aggregation; this exposes normalization effects. Then compare uniform aggregation, static learned softmax aggregation, and dynamic aggregation. Static weights are trainable depth biases shared across positions and users, initialized to zero. Dynamic gates use the same initial biases plus zero-initialized input-dependent weights. Match normalization, output scale, backbone, sampler, optimizer, validation schedule, and checkpoint policy across the aggregation variants. The baseline output pathway supplies the common scoring scale; do not add an ELMo-style extra scale only to selected variants. Static versus uniform tests learned depth preference; dynamic versus static tests conditioning; normalized final-depth versus baseline exposes the additional normalization change. None alone proves useful intent selection.

The initial report’s parameter-matched final-depth capacity control remains valuable but becomes conditional on budget after the essential normalization and static controls. Use a jointly trained positionwise bottleneck/projection with approximately matched extra parameters, the same normalization/output path, and documented measured compute; exact parameter and compute matching may be impossible. Report discrepancies rather than describing the control as perfectly matched. An optional retrained branch-detachment control uses detached intermediate outputs only at aggregation branches, retaining the final-depth branch and the backbone’s ordinary gradient path. Apply the detachment to both value and gate inputs for intermediate branches. It preserves initial forward access while removing their direct auxiliary gradient routes, but retraining changes backbone adaptation, so it does not isolate optimization perfectly. A position-only gate is a lower-priority control if a position feature is later introduced; the proposed initial gate has no explicit absolute-position input. Do not launch all controls automatically or combine their outputs.

Train each variant from the corrected cold start, using seed 42, and retain the same minibatch stream where the baseline permits a dedicated sampler RNG. Isolate sampler randomness from changes in parameter initialization so architectural changes do not silently alter training examples. Record exact parameters, peak memory, GPU seconds, optimizer updates, processed positions, convergence, validation queries, and checkpoint choices. Intermediate-state retention and normalization add training memory and compute even when gate parameters are few. Use the same prespecified per-trial GPU-time allowance and validation schedule for controlled comparisons, and report realized updates; equal time and equal updates cannot generally both be guaranteed. A time-capped variant is not an equal-epoch comparison. If the remaining shared budget cannot support essential controls, report that limitation and avoid claiming a demonstrated benefit from dynamic conditioning. Retain the baseline loss so this experiment isolates architecture. Multi-negative CE is a subsequent objective direction, not part of this initial proposal.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl with existing routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and account for all training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Four concurrent trial slots do not multiply that total allowance. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Select only by the unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10 protocol: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42. No hidden test access, additional datasets, pretrained weights, or evaluator changes are used. Each alternative is a separate single-model experiment. The selected predictor loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint for each of the four categories; no checkpoint averaging, score fusion, independently fitted transition/popularity components, or ensembles are introduced.

The supplied earlier combined_score=0.5537 is contextual evidence only, with no paired comparison establishing improvement for this architecture. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Gate conditioning can learn popularity, history-length, activation-norm, or user-specific shortcuts rather than current intent. Static weights can also suffice, or dynamic gates can converge to nearly constant weights. Keep the initial architecture and comparison order fixed, log every validation query, avoid open-ended normalization/gate sweeps, and freeze configuration before the separate held-out evaluation. No multi-seed experiment or checkpoint averaging is proposed. Report history-length breakdowns only when the unchanged host evaluator already provides them; do not construct substitute benchmark metrics from training pairs.

Preserve ModelView.model as the trained nn.Module and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. log2feats must return the aggregated B×L×D features used by actual scoring. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. Extend structural analysis to include intermediate-output branches, normalization, and gate dependencies through the shared softmax denominator; unsupported topology must produce an explicit unavailable result rather than a fabricated receptive-field claim. Item-category breakdowns remain unavailable because item categories are not provided. Dataset routing categories do not supply item-category annotations.

Retain existing finite, causal-invariance, prefix-equivalence, and view/network score checks. Add supported-position gate entropy, per-depth mean weights, and variability across rows and positions with explicit definitions and support counts; none establishes intent recognition. Record per-depth pre/post-normalization feature norms, weighted-value norms, and layerwise gradient norms at a small fixed set of training steps. Weighted-value norms still omit interactions and downstream scoring, so do not equate them with causal importance. For bounded gradient diagnostics, differentiate selected representations, logits, gates, and final scores with respect to input embedding outputs at chosen valid lags, not integer item IDs. Report support and acknowledge saturation and local linearity limitations. Repeated loader rows are not independent users; do not invent user-level uncertainty or identities.

Continue paired recent/older perturbations using identical candidates and support accounting. Besides the existing repacking versus embedding-ablation distinction, use fixed-position replacements of older valid items with permitted training-catalog IDs while preserving recent events, padding, and length. Such replacements and truncations can be out of distribution and do not establish naturally harmful context. On each supported original/perturbed pair, cache original values Z0 and weights A0, recompute Z1 and A1, and score S00=S(A0,Z0), S01=S(A0,Z1), S10=S(A1,Z0), and S11=S(A1,Z1) through the identical output normalization and scoring head. Report the value-path change S01−S00, routing-path change S10−S00, total S11−S00, and interaction S11−S10−S01+S00. These internal interventions need not correspond to realizable inputs or additive causal contributions. Report pairwise score changes on supplied diagnostic targets; report ranks only when a fixed permitted candidate set is actually available. Replacing gates with measured means is another inference perturbation, not a retrained ablation. Perturbed validation HR and user/history-length breakdowns require existing host support and must otherwise remain unavailable.

Continue diagnosis of the twenty real training users, five per category, using full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Track stale-interest rejection and broad-match rejection separately from unassessable items, and record relative ranks of explicitly preferred specific matches when the native diagnostic output supports them. Do not invent rejection rates from qualitative summaries. Compatibility, satisfied needs, and redundant substitutes remain unresolved: neither depth gates nor positive-only next-item supervision observes them directly. Use only permitted histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; this architecture needs no additional metadata. Reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, pretrained weights, and simulator diversity/conformity traits are unavailable regardless of the generic example schemas in the input.

Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical architecture, aggregation mode, normalization, configuration, checkpoint keys, mappings, and padding policy. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Read the final nonpadding position by positional maximum, never count−1; preserve the corrected baseline’s explicit empty-history policy without accidental −1 indexing. Verify generated-predictor reload scores on identical permitted inputs, category routing, mappings, truncation, padding, and candidate IDs in evaluation mode, including a small synthetic empty-history case. In-memory parity alone is insufficient. The existing diagnostic adapter has no reload interface, so keep deployment_reload_parity explicitly unavailable there unless a genuine host-compatible check is added; record separately measured export parity without claiming it from view/network agreement. Charge verification compute to the search budget.

Direct references missing from the original proposal are Jumping Knowledge Networks, ELMo, Dynamic Layer Aggregation, and SkipRec. They substantially reduce novelty claims. Mamba and FADC remain distant selection/context-control inspirations, not evidence that this architecture improves recommendation. Attention interpretation papers motivate intervention-based qualification, and Identity Mappings motivates the gradient-path alternative explanation. No new literature retrieval or independent verification was performed in this revision; literature descriptions rely on the supplied search material.
idea.pseudocode:
class DepthAggregation(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, width, depth_count, mode, baseline_norm_eps):
        super().__init__()
        assert mode in {'final', 'uniform', 'static', 'dynamic'}
        self.mode = mode
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(width, eps=baseline_norm_eps)
        # Construct only parameters actually used by each control.
        if mode in {'static', 'dynamic'}:
            self.gate_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(depth_count))
        if mode == 'dynamic':
            self.gate_weight = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(depth_count, width))

    def decompose(self, block_states, valid, detach_intermediate=False):
        # block_states: list of causal B x L x D tensors.
        # Optional retrained control: detach branch inputs, not backbone edges.
        states = [h.detach() if detach_intermediate and k < len(block_states)-1
                  else h for k, h in enumerate(block_states)]
        z = torch.stack([self.norm(h) for h in states], dim=2)
        z = z * valid[:, :, None, None]
        if self.mode == 'final':
            alpha = torch.zeros_like(z[..., 0])
            alpha[..., -1] = 1
        elif self.mode == 'uniform':
            alpha = torch.full_like(z[..., 0], 1.0 / z.shape[2])
        elif self.mode == 'static':
            alpha = self.gate_bias.softmax(dim=-1).expand(*z.shape[:3])
        else:
            logits = torch.einsum('blkd,kd->blk', z, self.gate_weight)
            alpha = (logits + self.gate_bias).softmax(dim=-1)
        return z, alpha

    def forward(self, block_states, valid, detach_intermediate=False):
        z, alpha = self.decompose(block_states, valid, detach_intermediate)
        mixed = (alpha[..., None] * z).sum(dim=2)
        return mixed * valid[..., None], alpha

# Integrate into the supplied NextItNet, preserving its actual block API.
def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    x = baseline_embedding_path(sequence) * valid[..., None]
    states = []
    for block in model.blocks:
        x = padding_safe_causal_block(block, x, valid)
        states.append(x)
    features, alpha = model.depth_aggregation(states, valid)
    return baseline_final_normalization(features) * valid[..., None]

# Corrected baseline reference bypasses this added aggregation/normalization.
# Train controls independently from cold start; never fuse scores/checkpoints.
# Training retains the family-specific sample_batch, baseline loss and target alignment.
# Use dedicated sampling RNG(seed=42) where supported; maximum 200 epochs,
# 200 batches/epoch; record concrete inherited baseline settings and GPU seconds.

# Inference: one full-history pass and one checkpoint per category.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
nonempty = last.ge(0)
scores[nonempty] = model.predict_score(
    features[nonempty, last[nonempty]], candidates[nonempty])
scores[~nonempty] = corrected_baseline_empty_history_policy(...)

# Bounded diagnostics in eval mode, using identical valid readouts/candidates.
# Z includes channel normalization; S includes the common final output pathway.
Z0, A0 = model.decompose_permitted_input(original_sequence)
Z1, A1 = model.decompose_permitted_input(perturbed_sequence)
S00 = score_mixed_features(A0, Z0, candidates)
S01 = score_mixed_features(A0, Z1, candidates)
S10 = score_mixed_features(A1, Z0, candidates)
S11 = score_mixed_features(A1, Z1, candidates)
report(value_change=S01-S00,
       routing_change=S10-S00,
       total_change=S11-S00,
       interaction=S11-S10-S01+S00,
       support=finite_supported_comparisons(...))
# These are internal interventions, not additive causal attribution.
# Preserve DiagnosisProbe, metrics/definitions, interpreter, and ModelView API.
# Export identical architecture/configuration; separately verify predictor reload.
# Baseline-specific helpers above are integration placeholders, not runnable APIs.

originality.positive: A diagnosis-directed transfer of established dynamic layer aggregation to a causal dilated-convolution recommender, with explicit normalization, static, and capacity controls.
originality.negative: Jumping Knowledge and Dynamic Layer Aggregation directly precede input-dependent softmax mixing across intermediate representations; SkipRec already studies adaptive depth within recommendation. This is an incremental adaptation.

future_potential.positive: A controlled study could distinguish context conditioning, static depth preference, normalization, and gradient-path effects, informing finer context selection while preserving NextItNet.
future_potential.negative: The module may behave like static aggregation or exploit popularity and history-length shortcuts, and benchmark gains would not demonstrate compatibility reasoning, current intent recognition, or a broadly new method.

code_difficulty.positive: The central module is small and preserves the existing backbone, item embeddings, scoring interface, and single-checkpoint deployment.
code_difficulty.negative: A defensible experiment requires normalization/static controls, padding correctness, intermediate-state memory management, dependency-aware diagnostics, bounded interventions, and generated-predictor parity. Missing baseline source prevents a complete drop-in implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal dilated residual convolution family retained by the proposed experiment.
Its intermediate convolutional depths motivate aggregation across contextual representations.
limitations: Does not establish that position-dependent depth gates improve this benchmark or infer current user purpose.
Receptive fields must be calculated from the corrected supplied implementation rather than assumed from a generic original block.

related_work.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
contributions: Provides a general precedent for input-dependent information selection.
limitations: Uses a different backbone; its results do not validate depth aggregation in NextItNet.
The experiment transfers a selection principle without adopting a state-space model.

related_work.title: On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax
contributions: The supplied search summary connects sampled-softmax optimization, temperature, and ranking performance.
Motivates a separate candidate-discrimination research direction.
limitations: Sampled objectives are surrogates for pinned HR@10 evaluation.
Changing the objective alongside depth aggregation would confound the architectural comparison.

related_work.title: Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution for Semantic Segmentation
contributions: Provides architectural inspiration for position-dependent control of convolutional context.
limitations: Evidence comes from vision and does not demonstrate recommendation gains.
Adaptive dilation differs from aggregating outputs of fixed causal dilation depths.

related_work.title: Representation Learning on Graphs with Jumping Knowledge Networks
contributions: Collects intermediate representations and aggregates them using concatenation, max pooling, or input-dependent attention.
Directly precedes adaptive aggregation over representations with different neighborhood ranges.
limitations: Graph neighborhoods differ from sequential causal receptive fields.
Does not establish recommendation gains or historical exclusion from learned weights.

related_work.title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
contributions: ELMo uses task-specific static softmax layer weights and an overall learned scale.
Provides the essential static aggregation comparison for testing input-dependent conditioning.
limitations: Its layer weights are shared across tokens, unlike the proposed dynamic gates.
Its language-model representations and training setting do not establish gains for NextItNet.

related_work.title: Dynamic Layer Aggregation for Neural Machine Translation
contributions: Includes a position-specific softmax combination of hidden layers using a feed-forward mechanism.
Provides an especially close precedent that materially limits the proposal’s originality.
limitations: Translation results do not establish improvements in sequential recommendation.
The proposed linear per-depth logits are a simpler adaptation, not a reproduction of all routing variants.

related_work.title: SkipRec: Streamlined and Scalable Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides related user-adaptive depth selection within sequential recommendation.
limitations: Selects or skips residual layers rather than pooling every intermediate output through softmax weights.
Its mechanism does not validate this proposed aggregation or its diagnostic interpretations.

related_work.title: Attention is not Explanation
contributions: Supports caution when interpreting attention or mixing weights as explanations of prediction dependence.
Motivates measuring score effects through interventions rather than weight magnitude alone.
limitations: Does not directly analyze this NextItNet module.
The shared-denominator dependency follows from the proposed computation itself, not an empirical result established by this reference.

related_work.title: Attention is not not Explanation
contributions: Motivates explicit criteria and intervention-based evaluation for explanatory claims.
limitations: Does not make gate weights sufficient evidence of historical exclusion.
Internal routing/value interventions require additional assumptions and need not represent naturally occurring inputs.

related_work.title: Understanding and Improving Layer Normalization
contributions: Supports treating normalization as an optimization intervention as well as a change in activation scale.
limitations: Does not establish which normalization arrangement is best for this benchmark.
Normalization can confound a claimed benefit from dynamic layer selection unless matched across controls.

related_work.title: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
contributions: Provides evidence for the optimization importance of direct signal and gradient propagation in residual networks.
Motivates investigating shorter loss-to-intermediate-layer paths as an alternative explanation for aggregation gains.
limitations: Does not establish that this aggregation improves optimization or recommendation.
A retrained branch-detachment control changes adaptation and cannot perfectly isolate one causal mechanism.
